questions.text: What is the remainder when 7<sup>100</sup> is divided by 5?
questions.solution: 7 leaves remainder 2 on division by 5, so 7^100 and 2^100 leave the same remainder. Powers of 2 cycle with period 4: 2, 4, 3, 1, 2, 4, 3, 1, ... Since 100 is a multiple of 4, 2^100 sits at the end of a cycle and leaves remainder 1.

questions.text: What is the HCF (greatest common divisor) of 1071 and 1044?
questions.solution: Euclid's algorithm: 1071 = 1044 x 1 + 27; 1044 = 27 x 38 + 18; 27 = 18 x 1 + 9; 18 = 9 x 2 + 0. The last non-zero remainder is 9.

questions.text: What is the least number which, when divided by 12, 15 and 20, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
questions.solution: A number leaving remainder 3 with each divisor is 3 more than a common multiple. LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60, so the least such number is 60 + 3 = 63.

questions.text: A number is first increased by 20% and the result is then decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
questions.solution: The multipliers compose: 1.20 x 0.80 = 0.96, so the number ends at 96% of what it was, a 4% decrease. Successive percentage changes multiply rather than add, which is why they do not cancel.

questions.text: The price of a commodity rises by 25%. By what percentage must a household reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on the commodity is unchanged?
questions.solution: Expenditure = price x consumption. If price becomes 1.25 times, consumption must become 1/1.25 = 0.8 times, a reduction of 20%.

questions.text: In an examination, 35% of candidates failed in Mathematics, 45% failed in English, and 20% failed in both. What percentage passed in both subjects?
questions.solution: Failed in at least one subject = 35 + 45 - 20 = 60%. Everyone else passed both, so 100 - 60 = 40%. Subtracting the overlap is what stops the 20% who failed both from being counted twice.

questions.text: If A is 25% more than B, then B is what percentage less than A?
questions.solution: Take B = 100, so A = 125. B falls short of A by 25, and that shortfall is measured against A: 25/125 = 20%. The base changes when the comparison is reversed, which is why the answer is not 25%.

questions.text: An article bought for Rs 400 is sold for Rs 500. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: Profit = 500 - 400 = 100, and profit percentage is measured on cost price: 100/400 = 25%.

questions.text: A trader sells an article at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for Rs 100 more, he would have made a profit of 10%. What is the cost price, in rupees?
questions.solution: Let the cost price be C. The two selling prices are 0.9C and 1.1C, and they differ by Rs 100. So 0.2C = 100 and C = 500.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above cost price and then allows a discount of 25% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution: Take cost = 100. Marked price = 140, and after 25% discount the selling price is 140 x 0.75 = 105. Profit = 5 on a cost of 100, so 5%.

questions.text: What is the simple interest, in rupees, on Rs 5000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years under simple interest. In how many years will it triple itself at the same rate?
questions.solution: Doubling means the interest earned equals the principal, so 8 years produce interest of P. Tripling needs interest of 2P, and simple interest accrues at a constant amount per year, so it takes 16 years.

questions.text: A sum lent at simple interest amounts to Rs 8100 in 3 years and to Rs 8400 in 4 years. What is the principal, in rupees?
questions.solution: The extra year adds 8400 - 8100 = Rs 300, so the annual interest is 300. Three years of interest is 900, and the principal is 8100 - 900 = 7200.

questions.text: What is the 7th term of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, 15, ... ?
questions.solution: a = 3 and d = 4, so the nth term is a + (n - 1)d = 3 + 6 x 4 = 27.

questions.text: What is the sum of the first 20 terms of an arithmetic progression whose first term is 5 and whose common difference is 3?
In an arithmetic progression the 4th term is 14 and the 10th term is 32. What is the common difference?
questions.solution: Six steps separate the 4th and 10th terms, so 6d = 32 - 14 = 18 and d = 3.

questions.text: A speed of 72 km/h is equal to how many metres per second?
questions.solution: Multiply by 5/18 to convert km/h to m/s: 72 x 5/18 = 20 m/s.

questions.text: A train 150 m long, travelling at 90 km/h, crosses a bridge 300 m long. How many seconds does it take?
questions.solution: To clear the bridge the train must cover its own length plus the bridge: 150 + 300 = 450 m. Its speed is 90 x 5/18 = 25 m/s, so the time is 450/25 = 18 s.

questions.text: A boat travels at 10 km/h in still water and the stream flows at 2 km/h. How many hours does the boat take to go 24 km downstream and return to its starting point?
questions.solution: Downstream speed is 12 km/h, taking 24/12 = 2 h. Upstream speed is 8 km/h, taking 24/8 = 3 h. Total 5 h.

questions.text: A car covers a distance at 40 km/h and returns along the same route at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution: Equal distances call for the harmonic mean: 2 x 40 x 60 / (40 + 60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h. The plain average of 50 would be right only if equal *times* were spent at each speed.

questions.text: A can finish a piece of work in 12 days and B can finish it in 18 days. Working together, how many days do they take? Give the answer to one decimal place.
questions.solution: Rates add: 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 of the work per day. The time is the reciprocal, 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.text: A and B together complete a task in 8 days. A alone would take 12 days. How long would B alone take?
questions.solution: B's rate is the combined rate minus A's: 1/8 - 1/12 = 3/24 - 2/24 = 1/24, so B alone takes 24 days.

questions.text: Twelve men can complete a project in 20 days. After 8 days of work, 4 men leave. How many days in total does the project take?
questions.solution: The project is 12 x 20 = 240 man-days. In 8 days, 12 x 8 = 96 man-days are done, leaving 144. With 8 men remaining that takes 144/8 = 18 more days, so 8 + 18 = 26 days in total.

questions.text: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B fills it in 4 hours. With both open, how many hours does the tank take to fill? Give the answer to one decimal place.
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/4 = 2/12 + 3/12 = 5/12 of the tank per hour, so the time is 12/5 = 2.4 hours.

questions.text: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours while pipe B can empty the full tank in 15 hours. If both are opened together on an empty tank, how long will it take to fill?
questions.solution: The outlet subtracts: 1/10 - 1/15 = 3/30 - 2/30 = 1/30 of the tank per hour. The net rate is positive, so the tank does fill, in 30 hours.

questions.text: Pipe A alone fills a tank in 20 minutes and pipe B alone in 30 minutes. Both are opened together, and A is closed after 5 minutes. How many minutes in total does the tank take to fill? Give the answer to one decimal place.
questions.solution: In the first 5 minutes the pipes fill 5 x (1/20 + 1/30) = 5 x 5/60 = 5/12 of the tank. The remaining 7/12 is left to B at 1/30 per minute, taking 7/12 x 30 = 17.5 minutes. Total = 5 + 17.5 = 22.5 minutes.

questions.text: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at exactly 3 o'clock?
questions.solution: Each hour mark is 360/12 = 30 degrees apart. At 3 o'clock the hands are three marks apart: 3 x 30 = 90 degrees.

questions.text: What is the angle, in degrees, between the hour hand and the minute hand at 4:20?
questions.solution: The minute hand is at 20 x 6 = 120 degrees. The hour hand has moved past 4 by a third of an hour: 4 x 30 + 20 x 0.5 = 130 degrees. The difference is 10 degrees. Forgetting that the hour hand drifts is what makes this look like 0.

questions.text: How many times do the hour and minute hands of a correct clock coincide in 24 hours?
questions.solution: The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours, not 12: between 11 o'clock and 1 o'clock there is only one coincidence, at 12. So 24 hours give 22.

questions.text: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the faces is 7?
questions.solution: Six of the 36 equally likely outcomes sum to 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). So the probability is 6/36 = 1/6, the most likely of all the sums.

questions.text: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are red? Give the answer correct to two decimal places.
questions.solution: P = (4/10) x (3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15, which is about 0.133. Equivalently C(4,2)/C(10,2) = 6/45. The second draw uses 3 and 9 because the first ball is not replaced.

questions.text: A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
questions.solution: Three of the eight equally likely sequences have exactly two heads: HHT, HTH, THH. So the probability is 3/8.

questions.text: Events A and B are independent, with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A union B)? Give the answer correct to one decimal place.
questions.solution: Independence gives P(A and B) = 0.4 x 0.5 = 0.2. Then P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.7. Adding without subtracting the overlap would wrongly give 0.9.

questions.text: A company's annual sales, in crore rupees, were: 2019 = 40, 2020 = 50, 2021 = 45, 2022 = 60. By what percentage did sales grow from 2019 to 2022?
questions.solution: The increase is 60 - 40 = 20 on a base of 40, so 20/40 = 50%.

questions.text: A company's annual sales, in crore rupees, were: 2019 = 40, 2020 = 50, 2021 = 45, 2022 = 60. What is the average annual sales figure over these four years, in crore rupees? Give the answer correct to two decimal places.
A company's annual sales, in crore rupees, were: 2019 = 40, 2020 = 50, 2021 = 45, 2022 = 60. In which year was the percentage increase over the previous year the largest?
questions.solution: 2020 grew by 10/40 = 25%, 2021 fell, and 2022 grew by 15/45 = 33.3%. The largest rise in absolute terms and in percentage terms are both 2022 here, but they need not coincide in general.

questions.text: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?
questions.solution: Their sum is 10 x 11/2 = 55, and 55/10 = 5.5. For consecutive numbers the average is also the midpoint of the first and last, (1 + 10)/2.

questions.text: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4. Six years from now the ratio will be 4 : 5. What is A's present age, in years?
questions.solution: Let the ages be 3x and 4x. Then (3x + 6)/(4x + 6) = 4/5, so 15x + 30 = 16x + 24 and x = 6. A is 3x = 18.

questions.text: The average of five numbers is 20. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 22. Which number was removed?
questions.solution: The five numbers total 5 x 20 = 100 and the remaining four total 4 x 22 = 88, so the number removed is 100 - 88 = 12.

questions.text: In a row of 40 students, Amit is 12th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.solution: Position from the right = total - position from the left + 1 = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29. The +1 is there because Amit is counted from both ends.

questions.text: In a class, Ravi ranks 7th from the top and 26th from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution: Total = 7 + 26 - 1 = 32. Ravi is counted in both ranks, so one is subtracted.

questions.text: In a row of children, Priya is 11th from the left and 15th from the right. How many children are in the row?
Given that A > B, B >= C and C > D, which of the following definitely follows?
questions.solution: The chain A > B >= C > D can be combined because every link points the same way, and a chain containing at least one strict inequality is strict overall. So A > D.

questions.text: Given the statement P >= Q = R < S, consider the conclusions: (I) P >= R  (II) S > Q. Which conclusions follow?
questions.solution: Q = R lets either symbol replace the other. P >= Q = R gives P >= R, and R < S with Q = R gives S > Q. Both hold.

questions.text: Given the statement M >= N > O <= P, consider the conclusions: (I) M > O  (II) M >= P. Which conclusions follow?
questions.solution: M >= N > O gives M > O. But the chain reverses direction at O <= P, so nothing links M to P: P could be enormous or barely above O. Only I follows.

questions.text: What comes next in the series 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ... ?
questions.solution: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12 and the next term is 42. Equivalently the nth term is n(n + 1): 6 x 7 = 42.

questions.text: What comes next in the series AZ, BY, CX, ... ?
questions.solution: The first letter advances A, B, C, D while the second retreats Z, Y, X, W. The pair is always a letter and its mirror in the alphabet, so DW.

questions.text: What comes next in the series 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ... ?
questions.solution: Each term is twice the previous one plus 1, so 63 x 2 + 1 = 127. Equivalently the terms are 2^n - 1: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 less one.

questions.text: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. A sits immediately to the left of B, D sits between B and E, and C sits at one end. Who sits at the other end?
questions.solution: A immediately left of B gives the block AB. D between B and E extends it to A B D E, four consecutive seats. C takes the only seat left, one end, so the block runs C A B D E and E is at the other end.

questions.text: P, Q, R and S sit around a circular table facing the centre. P sits directly opposite R, and Q sits immediately to the left of P. Who sits directly opposite Q?
questions.solution: With four people evenly spaced, each has exactly one person opposite. P and R take one pair of opposite seats, which leaves Q and S facing each other whichever side Q sits on.

questions.text: Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
questions.solution: The relation is professional to workplace. A doctor works in a hospital as a teacher works in a school. Student is the person served, not the place.

questions.text: Ignite : Extinguish :: Enter : ?
questions.solution: The pair is an antonym pair: to ignite is the opposite of to extinguish, and to enter is the opposite of to exit. Arrive and admit are near-synonyms of enter, not opposites.

questions.text: Cartographer : Map :: Choreographer : ?
questions.solution: The relation is maker to the thing made. A cartographer makes maps; a choreographer composes dances. Stage is where it happens, and chorus is a false lead from the spelling.

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: "Each of the students ___ submitted the assignment."
questions.solution: The subject is "each", which is singular; "of the students" is a prepositional phrase and never governs the verb. So the verb is "has".

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: "Neither the manager nor the employees ___ satisfied with the decision."
questions.solution: With "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Employees" is plural and stands closest, so "were" is correct. Reversing the order would make "was" correct.

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: "The list of approved items ___ on the noticeboard."
questions.solution: The subject is "the list", singular. "Of approved items" is a modifier, and a plural noun inside it does not change the number of the subject.

questions.text: Choose the correct article: "She is ___ honest officer."
questions.solution: The choice between a and an follows the opening *sound*, not the letter. The h in honest is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound and takes "an".

questions.text: Choose the correct article: "___ Ganga is the longest river in India."
questions.solution: Names of rivers, seas, mountain ranges and groups of islands take the definite article, unlike names of individual mountains or lakes.

questions.text: Choose the correct pair of articles: "He is ___ university professor and ___ MBA graduate."
questions.solution: University begins with a consonant sound, "yoo", so it takes "a". MBA is read as a letter, "em", which begins with a vowel sound, so it takes "an". Both are decided by sound rather than spelling.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive form of: "The committee approved the proposal."

options.text: The proposal was approved by the committee.
The proposal is approved by the committee.
The proposal had approved by the committee.
The proposal has been approving by the committee.

questions.solution: The object becomes the subject, and the simple past "approved" becomes "was approved". The tense must be preserved when the voice changes.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive form of: "Someone has stolen my bicycle."

options.text: My bicycle was stolen by someone.

questions.solution: Present perfect becomes "has been + past participle". An indefinite agent like "someone" is normally dropped, which is one of the reasons the passive is used at all.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive form of: "They are building a new bridge across the river."

options.text: A new bridge is being built across the river.
A new bridge is built across the river.
A new bridge was being built across the river.
A new bridge has been building across the river.

questions.solution: The present continuous becomes "is/are being + past participle", so "are building" becomes "is being built" to match the singular subject "bridge".
